hook_text: One hundred people, one loaf. Walk past sixty of them — you've counted a tenth of the bread.
clip_script: Line up one hundred people from thinnest slice to thickest, and stroll down the line keeping a running total of bread. In a perfectly fair country your total rises steadily — half the bread by person fifty. In ours, you pass person sixty still holding barely a tenth of the loaf, while the final handful at the end of the line hold roughly half of it between them. Your stroll just traced the Lorenz curve — and the number that scores it, from zero for perfect equality to one for one-person-takes-all, hovers near nought comma six five here: about the deepest sag any country has ever measured. So the state moves bread back along the line with five hands: taxes that cut thicker slices from thicker plates, grants landing where plates are thinnest, free basic water and power, a floor under wages, and moving the ovens themselves. Every hand works, and every hand has a blister. Grow the loaf AND move the shares — anyone arguing only one has half an argument.
visual_style: A hundred simple figures holding plates that thicken along the line; a walking tally ticking up painfully slowly, then leaping at the end; the tally drawn as a deep sag under a straight diagonal; five hands passing bread back down the queue.
mood: Sober arithmetic that turns purposeful — the numbers sting, the five hands answer.
pacing: A slow deliberate walk with the tally, a silent beat at person sixty, brisk beats for the five hands, firm two-armed close.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep: the loaf, the medical chart, the one-world shop and the seed mealies.
